### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A19, A20, A25 and A26 are not observed at all; in the later window each takes part in roughly 20–30 in 100 traces (41–61 of 200 cases). They almost never share a trace (co-occurrence below 1 in 100), so they behave as mutually exclusive alternatives. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL016, REL017, REL025, REL033]

- The four occur near the middle of the trace (mean relative position about 0.51–0.52). Order relations place them after A28 (A28 precedes each in about 20–30 in 100 traces) and before A30 (each precedes A30 in about 20–30 in 100 traces), and their observed outgoing transitions split roughly evenly between A29 and A30. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, REL019, REL027, REL034, REL041, REL021, REL029, REL036, REL043, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]

- Routing around them changed accordingly: A28's outgoing transitions, previously about 99 in 100 towards A29, now send about 12–13 in 100 to each of the four; A29's share towards A30 fell from about 96 in 100 to 51 in 100, with new outgoing edges to the four (about 7–16 in 100 each). [DIR007, DIR008]

- Neighbouring event gaps stretched by about one position: A28→A29 moved from lag 1 in almost all cases to lag 1 and lag 2 in roughly equal shares; A28→A30 from lag 2 (about 97 in 100) to lag 3 (about 97 in 100); A29→A30 from lag 1 (about 97 in 100) to lag 1 and lag 2 in about equal shares. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]

- A04 participation tripled, from 10 in 100 traces (20 cases) to 28 in 100 (56 cases), with mean occurrences per trace rising from about 0.1 to 0.3 and its mean relative position moving earlier, from about 0.58 to 0.21. In the later window A04 directly follows A14 in 96 in 100 of observed pairs (48 of 50; before, 2 of 3), the A14→A04 transition share rose from about 1 in 100 to 24 in 100, and A04's observed outgoing transitions go to A15 in 83 in 100 of cases (about 10 in 100 before, then spread over many targets; 21 transitions observed before, 59 after). A04 now precedes A28 in about 25 in 100 traces (about 5 in 100 before) and each of the four in about 5–8 in 100 traces. [OCC001, POS001, LAG001, DIR002, DIR001, REL005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]

- Smaller shifts also qualified: A30's mean position moved slightly later (about 0.55 to 0.56), and lag and routing distributions around A43–A47 and A45/A46 redistributed modestly. [POS006, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, DIR009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The screening produced 74 evidence items against roughly 1 expected if nothing had changed (0.95 over 190 units), a count chance cannot explain as a whole. Within that, the evidence directly and consistently supports the possibility that, in the later window, many traces run an additional mid-process step chosen from A19, A20, A25 and A26 — one alternative per trace — placed after A28 (sometimes after A29) and before A30, with onward flow to A29 or A30. The placement rests on order and adjacency evidence, not participation alone: A28 and A29 gained outgoing edges to the four while their direct edges towards A29/A30 shrank, A28 precedes and A30 follows the four in about 20–30 in 100 traces, and the A28→A29, A28→A30 and A29→A30 gaps stretched by about one event position. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL016, REL025, DIR007, DIR008, REL019, REL034, REL021, REL036, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004]

A second, behaviourally distinct shift is the heavier and earlier use of A04: from a rare, later-placed activity (10 in 100 traces) to one in about 28 in 100 traces that typically sits directly between A14 and A15, and which precedes the new mid-process step in a minority of traces. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004]

Limitations: the windows are finite samples, so the competing explanation that these four activities belong to a pre-existing rare variant that happened not to appear among the 200 earlier traces cannot be fully excluded, although 0 of 200 earlier versus 41–61 of 200 later makes a pure sampling difference unlikely; the smaller shifts around A30 and A43–A47 may be sampling noise; and many items rest on the same traces (for example the relation items pairing each new activity with A28, A29 and A30), so they describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. [OCC002, OCC005, POS006, LAG005, REL019, REL020, REL021]
